narrativeReportMd:
# Distance R4-to-R6 breaking-change assessment

## Bottom line
No local hard instance-breaking change was found for `Distance`. R4 and R6 keep the same artifact identity, base type, element list, cardinalities, primitive types, modifier and summary flags, local distance-unit invariant, primary binding, and distance-unit code compose.

## Scope
This report is scoped to local `Distance` changes. Inherited `Quantity`, `Element`, `DataType`, and `Extension` changes are excluded from `findings[]`; the most important inherited issue is the R6 `Quantity.comparator` code `ad`, which can affect Distance instances but belongs in the `Quantity` analysis.

## Main migration themes
Distance instance data generally does not need a Distance-specific transform. The local migration risk is for validators, code generators, and conformance tooling that read raw StructureDefinition JSON: the maximum distance-unit binding moved from the R4 `elementdefinition-maxValueSet` extension to the R6 `ElementDefinition.binding.additional` representation. Tooling also needs to keep inherited Quantity migration rules separate from Distance-local changes.

## Highest-impact findings
There are no Critical or High local findings. The only local finding is a Low-impact StructureDefinition metadata conversion risk around the maximum unit binding representation.

## Findings requiring human review
No local finding requires human review. Reviewers should still check the separate `Quantity` report before planning Distance migration because inherited comparator and UCUM-warning changes can affect validators and R6-to-R4 conversion of Distance values.

## Backward-compatible design observations
The R6 metadata form appears to formalize an R4 extension rather than change the Distance value domain. Keeping the old extension in parallel could have helped older tooling, but the instance-level semantics are preserved.

## Follow-up analysis
Analyze `Quantity` for inherited comparator and invariant changes, and run terminology expansion if precise UCUM distance-unit coverage is needed.

summary.executiveSummaryMd: No local hard instance-breaking change was found for `Distance`. The main local migration concern is a Low-impact StructureDefinition metadata representation change for the maximum distance-unit value set; inherited `Quantity` changes, especially comparator code `ad`, must be reviewed separately. Confidence is high for StructureDefinition deltas and medium for terminology expansion effects because UCUM expansions were not supplied.
summary.migrationThemesMd: Distance instance payloads remain structurally stable: the same elements, cardinalities, primitive types, modifier and summary flags, root binding strength, and Distance-specific invariant are present. Migration work is mostly in validators and model tooling: update R6 StructureDefinition readers to understand `binding.additional[purpose=maximum]`, do not infer a Distance-local comparator change, and keep inherited Quantity migration rules separate.
summary.confidenceSummaryMd: Confidence is high for the local StructureDefinition comparison because both assigned StructureDefinitions were present and their snapshots and differentials were compared. Confidence is lower for exhaustive terminology semantics because the supplied ValueSets did not include expansions, especially for the UCUM-filtered `all-distance-units` maximum value set. Confidence in rationale is also limited by the absence of an official Distance-specific diff or ballot change note.

findings.title: Distance maximum unit value set moved from R4 maxValueSet extension to R6 binding.additional

oldState.summary: The root Distance binding used extensible ValueSet/distance-units and represented the maximum permitted unit set with the R4 elementdefinition-maxValueSet extension.

terminologyComparison.terminologyNotesMd: The R4 primary distance-units ValueSet compose contains UCUM codes `nm`, `um`, `mm`, `m`, and `km`. The maximum all-distance-units ValueSet compose uses a UCUM `canonical = m` filter. No expansion was run.

oldState.narrativeMd: In R4, the Distance differential carries `binding.valueSet = http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/distance-units` and an extension `http://hl7.org/fhir/StructureDefinition/elementdefinition-maxValueSet` pointing at `http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/all-distance-units`.

newState.summary: The root Distance binding keeps the same extensible primary ValueSet but represents the maximum unit set with ElementDefinition.binding.additional purpose maximum.

terminologyComparison.terminologyNotesMd: R6 keeps the same primary distance-units ValueSet URL and uses `binding.additional[{purpose: maximum}]` for all-distance-units. The R6 distance-units compose still lists `nm`, `um`, `mm`, `m`, and `km`.

newState.narrativeMd: In R6, the same maximum value set is expressed as `binding.additional` with `purpose = maximum` and `valueSet = http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/all-distance-units`.

facts.note: The primary extensible binding identity did not change.
R4 used an extension to express the maximum binding.
R6 uses the core additional binding structure.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The same root `Distance` element and the same primary and maximum value-set URLs are present in both versions; only the metadata representation of the maximum binding changed.

impact.impactRationaleMd: This does not make an R4 Distance instance invalid in R6: the primary extensible binding and maximum value-set URL are preserved, and the common distance-unit code compose is unchanged. The risk is for validators, code generators, or conformance tooling that read raw StructureDefinition JSON. R4-specific tools that only search for the `elementdefinition-maxValueSet` extension can miss the R6 maximum binding; R6-to-R4 metadata conversion must map `binding.additional[purpose=maximum]` back to the R4 extension if an R4-shaped StructureDefinition is required.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: The likely failure mode is under- or over-enforcement of acceptable Distance units by tooling, not loss of clinical or measurement values in normal instance exchange.

justification.inferredGoal: Promote a formerly extension-based maximum binding into the standard R6 ElementDefinition binding model.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: R6 could have retained the R4 maxValueSet extension alongside binding.additional for maximum bindings, but only as duplicate legacy metadata.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The inferred R6 goal is reasonable: a formerly extension-based maximum binding became part of the core `ElementDefinition.binding.additional` model while preserving the same primary and maximum value-set URLs. This is not a Distance instance-shape break, and the impact is limited to validators, code generators, and conversion tooling that read raw StructureDefinition metadata. A less-breaking base design was possible, but it would have required keeping the old extension in parallel with the new first-class field, so the remaining breakage is probably justified.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The best less-breaking base R6 design would have emitted both `binding.additional[{purpose: "maximum"}]` and the old `elementdefinition-maxValueSet` extension for this maximum binding. That would preserve most R4-era metadata consumers while still introducing the R6 core representation. The alternative is only partial because it duplicates the same conformance fact, requires the two representations to stay synchronized, does not cover the richer R6 additional-binding model beyond the legacy maximum-binding case, and risks legacy extension use accumulating indefinitely instead of disappearing.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Dual representation would help older StructureDefinition tooling but creates synchronization risk and could prolong reliance on a deprecated extension pattern.

evidence.detail: R4 Distance uses elementdefinition-maxValueSet to identify the maximum distance-unit ValueSet.
R6 Distance uses binding.additional with purpose maximum for the same ValueSet.
The primary binding remains extensible to ValueSet/distance-units.
The primary binding remains extensible to ValueSet/distance-units.
The explicit primary distance-units code list is unchanged: nm, um, mm, m, and km.

examples.examplesMd: The example is a StructureDefinition binding metadata transform, not a Distance instance transform.

findings.narrativeMd: The Distance-specific unit binding semantics are preserved, but the way the maximum allowable unit set is represented changed. This matters for validators and code generators that inspect StructureDefinition JSON rather than using a version-aware FHIR model. An R4-only reader may look for the R4 extension and conclude that R6 Distance has no maximum binding unless it is updated to read `binding.additional`.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: There is no old-valid/new-invalid Distance instance solely because of this change. Correct R6 validation should still apply the same primary extensible distance-unit binding and the same maximum all-distance-units concept. The compatibility issue is metadata-level: R6 StructureDefinition content is not naively R4-shaped, and an R6-to-R4 StructureDefinition conversion must translate the additional binding back to the R4 extension to preserve validation semantics.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Update validators, code generators, and StructureDefinition conversion scripts to map R4 `elementdefinition-maxValueSet` and R6 `binding.additional[purpose=maximum]` as equivalent facts. Add tests that read both R4 and R6 Distance definitions and verify that the maximum value-set URL remains `http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/all-distance-units`.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The change was likely part of a general R6 improvement to make additional bindings first-class. A backward-compatible alternative would have been to emit both the new core representation and the old extension for at least one release, but that would duplicate metadata and require consistency checks.

checkedNoMaterialChange.notesMd: `Distance` remains `http://hl7.org/fhir/StructureDefinition/Distance`, id `Distance`, kind `complex-type`, type `Distance`, non-abstract, and a specialization of `Quantity`.
Both snapshots contain the same eight element ids: `Distance`, `Distance.id`, `Distance.extension`, `Distance.value`, `Distance.comparator`, `Distance.unit`, `Distance.system`, and `Distance.code`.
All snapshot min/max cardinalities match between R4 and R6 for the Distance snapshot: root `0..*`, `extension` `0..*`, and all other child elements `0..1`.

The element type codes are unchanged: `decimal` for `Distance.value`, `code` for `Distance.comparator` and `Distance.code`, `string` for `Distance.unit`, `uri` for `Distance.system`, `Extension` for `Distance.extension`, and FHIRPath string for `Distance.id`.
`Distance` has no Reference-typed elements or targetProfile lists.

The local root binding strength and primary value-set URL are unchanged, and the explicit `distance-units` compose contains the same five UCUM codes. The maximum `all-distance-units` binding URL is also unchanged, but its StructureDefinition representation changed and is reported separately.

The Distance-local invariant `dis-1` keeps severity `error`, the same human text, and the same FHIRPath expression requiring a code when value exists and UCUM system when system is present. New or changed inherited Quantity/Element/Extension constraints are out of scope.
No Distance element has a fixed, pattern, or default value in either version.
No minValue, maxValue, maxLength, or regex limit is introduced or changed locally for Distance.

`Distance.comparator` remains a modifier through its inherited Quantity definition, and the other Distance snapshot elements keep their modifier status. Inherited comparator semantics are delegated to the `Quantity` report.
Summary flags are unchanged for the Distance snapshot elements: `value`, `comparator`, `unit`, `system`, and `code` are summary elements; `id` and `extension` are not.
The only slicing visible in the Distance snapshot is inherited open slicing of `Distance.extension` by `url`; its discriminator and rules are unchanged.
The root short, definition, and comment text are unchanged. Top-level description wording drops the R4 boilerplate prefix `Base StructureDefinition for`, which does not change conformance semantics.
No Distance instance JSON/XML element serialization change was found. StructureDefinition metadata serialization changed for the maximum binding and is captured as the local finding.

No local Distance element was added that would make R6 Distance instances unrepresentable in R4. The inherited R6 `Quantity.comparator` code `ad` can create an R6-to-R4 representability issue for Distance instances, but that is owned by the `Quantity` analysis.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: Distance conformance maturity/status advanced
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: R4 `Distance` has StructureDefinition status `draft` and standards-status `trial-use`; R6 has status `active` and standards-status `normative`. This does not change instance shape or validation rules.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Governance, documentation, and conformance tooling may treat R6 Distance as more stable. Do not interpret this as a local data transform requirement.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R6 adds Distance type-characteristic metadata
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: R6 adds StructureDefinition type-characteristic extensions for `has-range`, `is-continuous`, and `has-units`. These describe the datatype for tooling but do not add or remove instance elements, constraints, or bindings.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Model analyzers and documentation generators may expose these characteristics in R6. R4 data does not need transformation because the extensions are artifact metadata.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: Common distance-unit codes stayed the same while ValueSet metadata changed
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: Both R4 and R6 `ValueSet/distance-units` include the same UCUM codes `nm`, `um`, `mm`, `m`, and `km` with the same displays. R6 changes metadata such as ValueSet status, standards status, publisher, jurisdiction, and description wording; membership of the explicit compose list is unchanged.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Systems that compare ValueSet resource metadata may see changed labels or status. Validation should key on system and code, and terminology-sensitive systems should use a terminology expansion if exact UCUM coverage matters.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: Distance-local invariant keeps the same FHIRPath while R4 XPath metadata is absent in R6
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: The Distance-local invariant `dis-1` has the same severity, human text, and FHIRPath expression in both versions. R6 no longer carries the R4 XPath expression in the constraint component and adds a `source` URI.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: XPath-only validation tooling should migrate to the FHIRPath expression. This is a tooling migration note rather than a Distance instance validity change because the authoritative FHIRPath rule is unchanged.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: Root RIM mapping presentation changed in the snapshot
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: The R4 Distance root snapshot included an additional terse RIM mapping entry `PQ` alongside the more descriptive Quantity-derived mapping. The R6 root snapshot shows the descriptive RIM mapping, while the local differential still includes the terse `PQ` mapping. These mappings are informative metadata and do not affect instance validation.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Mapping-documentation generators may produce slightly different root mapping output, but no Distance instance conversion rule was removed from the computable element model.

followUpDependencies.reasonMd: `Distance` specializes `Quantity`; inherited R6 changes include the required comparator value set adding code `ad`, the inherited best-practice warning `qty-4`, and the `Quantity` baseDefinition moving through `DataType`. These can affect Distance validators and R6-to-R4 conversion but are not local Distance findings.
